q: Write an algorithm in pseudocode that receives **two** numbers from the keyboard, then displays their sum and their average. (4)
ms: Both inputs received (1); sum calculated correctly (1); average = sum / 2 (1); both results output (1).
msCode:
RECEIVE a FROM KEYBOARD
RECEIVE b FROM KEYBOARD
SET sum TO a + b
SET avg TO sum / 2
SEND sum TO DISPLAY
SEND avg TO DISPLAY

q: Write an algorithm that receives a temperature in Celsius and displays **"Freezing"** if it is 0 or below, otherwise displays **"Above freezing"**. (4)
ms: Input received (1); correct condition temp <= 0 (1); correct message on the true branch (1); ELSE with the other message (1).
msCode:

IF temp <= 0 THEN
   SEND "Freezing" TO DISPLAY
ELSE
   SEND "Above freezing" TO DISPLAY

q: Write a **validation** algorithm that asks for a percentage and keeps asking until the value is between 0 and 100 inclusive. It should then display "Accepted". (5)

   RECEIVE percent FROM KEYBOARD
UNTIL (percent >= 0) AND (percent <= 100)
SEND "Accepted" TO DISPLAY

q: Write an algorithm that receives numbers until the sentinel **-1** is entered, then displays how many numbers were entered (not counting the -1) and their total. (6)
ms: count and total initialised to 0 (1); first number received before the loop OR loop structured so -1 is not counted (1); WHILE num <> -1 (1); total and count updated inside the loop (1); next number received at the end of the loop body (1); both results displayed after the loop (1).
msCode:
SET count TO 0
SET total TO 0
RECEIVE num FROM KEYBOARD
WHILE num <> -1 DO
   SET total TO total + num
   SET count TO count + 1
   RECEIVE num FROM KEYBOARD
END WHILE
SEND count TO DISPLAY
SEND total TO DISPLAY

q: Write an algorithm that receives **20** numbers and displays the **largest** one. (5)
ms: First number received and used to initialise max (1); loop for the remaining 19 (accept 20 with sensible handling) (1); each number compared with max (1); max updated when the new number is bigger (1); max displayed after the loop (1).
msCode:
RECEIVE max FROM KEYBOARD
FOR i FROM 2 TO 20 DO
   RECEIVE num FROM KEYBOARD
   IF num > max THEN
      SET max TO num
   END IF
END FOR
SEND max TO DISPLAY

q: Write an algorithm that receives a number of **minutes** and displays it as whole hours and remaining minutes, e.g. 130 → 2 hours 10 minutes. (4)

SET hours TO mins DIV 60
SET remmins TO mins MOD 60
SEND hours & " hours " & remmins & " minutes" TO DISPLAY

q:
A shop gives a discount: spend £100 or more → 20% off; spend £50 to £99.99 → 10% off; otherwise no discount.

Write an algorithm that receives the amount spent and displays the final price. (5)
ms: Input received (1); first check spend >= 100 with 20% applied (price = spend * 0.8) (1); ELSE IF spend >= 50 with 10% (1); ELSE price unchanged (1); final price displayed (1).
msCode:
RECEIVE spend FROM KEYBOARD
IF spend >= 100 THEN
   SET price TO spend * 0.8
ELSE IF spend >= 50 THEN
   SET price TO spend * 0.9
ELSE
   SET price TO spend
END IF
SEND price TO DISPLAY

q: Write an algorithm that counts down from **10 to 1**, displaying each number, then displays "Lift off!". (4)

END FOR

q: Write an algorithm that receives **15** numbers and displays how many of them were **even**. (5)

q:
A car park charges £2.50 per hour for the first 3 hours and £1.00 per hour for every additional hour.

Write an algorithm that receives the number of whole hours parked and displays the charge. (5)
ms: Input received (1); selection on hours <= 3 (1); simple case: hours * 2.50 (1); otherwise 3 * 2.50 + (hours - 3) * 1.00 (1); charge displayed (1).
msCode:
RECEIVE hours FROM KEYBOARD
IF hours <= 3 THEN
   SET charge TO hours * 2.50
ELSE
   SET charge TO 7.50 + (hours - 3) * 1.00
END IF
SEND charge TO DISPLAY

q: Write an algorithm that receives exam marks until **-1** is entered, then displays the **average** mark. If no marks were entered, it should display "No marks" instead. (6)
ms: total and count initialised (1); sentinel loop that excludes -1 from the data (1); total and count updated per mark (1); after the loop, check count > 0 (1); average = total / count displayed when count > 0 (1); "No marks" displayed otherwise (1).
msCode:
SET total TO 0
SET count TO 0
RECEIVE mark FROM KEYBOARD
WHILE mark <> -1 DO
   SET total TO total + mark
   SET count TO count + 1
   RECEIVE mark FROM KEYBOARD
END WHILE
IF count > 0 THEN
   SEND total / count TO DISPLAY
ELSE
   SEND "No marks" TO DISPLAY
END IF

q: Write an algorithm that receives a whole number and displays **"Multiple of 5"**, **"Multiple of 2"**, or **"Neither"**. A number that is a multiple of both should display only "Multiple of 5". (5)
ms: Input received (1); first test num MOD 5 = 0 (1); ELSE IF num MOD 2 = 0 (1); ELSE branch for "Neither" (1); tests in the stated priority order so multiples of 10 show "Multiple of 5" (1).
msCode:
RECEIVE num FROM KEYBOARD
IF num MOD 5 = 0 THEN
   SEND "Multiple of 5" TO DISPLAY
ELSE IF num MOD 2 = 0 THEN
   SEND "Multiple of 2" TO DISPLAY
ELSE
   SEND "Neither" TO DISPLAY
END IF

q:
This search displays "Found" if the target is in the 100-item list, but always checks all 100 items.

Rewrite the loop so it stops as soon as the target is found, and state why this is more efficient. (3)
code:
SET found TO FALSE
FOR i FROM 1 TO 100 DO
   IF list(i) = target THEN
      SET found TO TRUE
   END IF
END FOR
ms: A condition-controlled loop replaces the fixed FOR, e.g. WHILE (found = FALSE) AND (i <= 100) (2 — 1 for loop choice, 1 for correct compound condition); efficiency: on average far fewer comparisons because it exits when the target is found (1).
msCode:
SET found TO FALSE
SET i TO 1
WHILE (found = FALSE) AND (i <= 100) DO
   IF list(i) = target THEN
      SET found TO TRUE
   END IF
   SET i TO i + 1
END WHILE

q: Write an algorithm for a guessing game: the secret number is 42. The player keeps guessing; after each wrong guess display "Higher" or "Lower" as a hint, and display "Correct" with the number of guesses when they get it. (5)

q:
A school tuck shop needs a till algorithm.

Requirements: receive item prices until 0 is entered; total the prices; if the total is over £10, apply a 5% discount; receive the cash given; display the total charged and the change.

Write the algorithm in pseudocode. (6)
ms: total initialised to 0 (1); sentinel loop on 0 collecting and summing prices (1); discount selection: IF total > 10 THEN total * 0.95 (1); cash received after the loop (1); change = cash - total calculated (1); total and change both displayed (1).
msCode:
SET total TO 0
RECEIVE price FROM KEYBOARD
WHILE price <> 0 DO
   SET total TO total + price
   RECEIVE price FROM KEYBOARD
END WHILE
IF total > 10 THEN
   SET total TO total * 0.95
END IF
RECEIVE cash FROM KEYBOARD
SET change TO cash - total
SEND "Total: " & total TO DISPLAY
SEND "Change: " & change TO DISPLAY
